stories.title: Trezor, BitBox warn users about fake hardware wallet security alerts
stories.summary: Trezor and BitBox told customers to watch for fake security alerts. Scammers send these alerts to trick wallet owners into acting. Both companies urged users to verify any alert before responding.
stories.whyItMatters: Hardware wallet users hold their own private keys, so a convincing fake alert can lead directly to stolen funds.
whatToWatch: Official guidance from Trezor and BitBox on how to spot real alerts
Reports of losses tied to the fake alerts
questions: How did scammers get the contact details to send these alerts?
Are other hardware wallet makers targeted too?

sources.title: Trezor, BitBox warn users about fake hardware wallet security alerts

stories.title: Consensys to split into MetaMask and an institutional blockchain company
stories.summary: Consensys plans to split into two separate companies. One will center on MetaMask, its widely used wallet. The other will focus on institutional blockchain clients.
stories.whyItMatters: MetaMask is one of the most used crypto wallets, so a corporate split could change its funding, governance, or product direction.
whatToWatch: The official timeline and names of the two new companies
Any changes to MetaMask's service for existing users
questions: Will MetaMask's governance or token plans change under the split?
Which Consensys businesses move to the institutional side?

stories.title: Bitcoin sell pressure hits one-month low as long-term holders ease off
stories.summary: On-chain data shows bitcoin sell pressure at its lowest point in a month. Long-term holders have slowed their profit-taking. Separately, CryptoSlate reported on a case where 4,100 stolen bitcoin funded a lifestyle of private jets and supercars.
stories.whyItMatters: Slower selling by long-term holders removes one source of downward price pressure, a factor traders track closely.
whatToWatch: Whether long-term holder sell pressure keeps falling
Updates on the stolen-bitcoin case
questions: What caused long-term holders to slow their selling now?
What happens to the stolen 4,100 bitcoin, and to the person who spent it?

How 4,100 stolen Bitcoin bankrolled a life of private jets and supercars

stories.title: Treasury's $6 billion bond intervention sets up a test for bitcoin
stories.summary: The US Treasury made a $6 billion intervention in the bond market. CryptoSlate frames this as a hidden test of bitcoin's next move, given the links between bond markets and risk assets. Details on the intervention itself are limited in this report.
stories.whyItMatters: Bond market moves affect liquidity and risk appetite, and both can spill over into bitcoin's price.
whatToWatch: Bitcoin's price action in the days after the intervention
Any further Treasury market moves
questions: What exactly did the Treasury intervention involve, and why now?
How closely has bitcoin actually tracked recent bond market moves?

stories.title: Trezor says hackers breached its email provider
stories.summary: Trezor, the hardware wallet maker, said hackers breached its email service provider. The company disclosed the breach to warn users about possible phishing risk.
stories.whyItMatters: A breach of a wallet maker's email channel raises phishing risk for self-custody users, who are frequent targets because they control their own keys.
whatToWatch: Trezor's guidance on spotting phishing emails tied to the breach
Confirmation of how many users were affected
questions: Was any wallet or key data exposed, or only email contact information?
Which email provider was breached?

stories.title: U.S. Bank tests proprietary stablecoin in cross-border Stellar transaction
stories.summary: U.S. Bank tested its own stablecoin in a cross-border transaction on the Stellar network. The test shows continued bank interest in using public blockchains for payments.
stories.whyItMatters: Bank-issued stablecoins on public chains could reshape cross-border payments and add competition for existing stablecoin issuers.
whatToWatch: Whether the test expands into live, production transactions
Other banks launching similar stablecoin pilots
questions: Is this stablecoin meant for retail use, or only bank-to-bank settlement?
What is the timeline to a live rollout?

stories.title: Ethereum institutional staking grows, but Lido's market share shrinks
stories.summary: Institutional staking of ethereum keeps growing. But Lido, the largest liquid staking provider, is losing market share as competition increases.
stories.whyItMatters: Staking concentration affects ethereum's decentralization, so a shift away from the dominant provider matters for network security debates.
whatToWatch: Which providers are gaining the share Lido is losing
Total ethereum staked levels in coming weeks
questions: Which specific competitors are taking share from Lido?
Is the shift driven by institutional preference for other providers?

stories.title: US sanctions Xinbi scam marketplace, restrains $52 million in crypto
stories.summary: The US government sanctioned Xinbi, a marketplace linked to scams. Authorities also restrained $52 million in crypto tied to the platform.
stories.whyItMatters: This is a concrete enforcement action against scam infrastructure, showing regulators can trace and freeze illicit crypto funds at scale.
whatToWatch: Related indictments or arrests tied to Xinbi
Whether similar marketplaces face action next
questions: Who operated Xinbi, and where were they based?
Will the restrained funds reach scam victims?

stories.title: Bitcoin fails to reclaim $80K as Bessent comments fuel yen strength
stories.summary: Bitcoin failed to reclaim the $80,000 level. Comments from Treasury Secretary Bessent helped push the yen stronger, trading around 153 per dollar. The stronger yen weighed on risk assets, including bitcoin.
stories.whyItMatters: Currency and macro moves are increasingly tied to bitcoin's price, so Treasury commentary and FX shifts matter to crypto traders.
whatToWatch: Whether bitcoin retests the $80K level
Further yen moves or follow-up comments from Bessent
questions: Is the yen strength likely to persist or fade quickly?
How much of bitcoin's stall is yen-driven versus other factors?

stories.title: Hunter Biden's LAPTOP memecoin promised to fix grift, made new losers instead
stories.summary: Hunter Biden launched a memecoin called LAPTOP. He pitched it as an antidote to memecoin grift. CryptoSlate reports it instead produced a new round of losing traders.
stories.whyItMatters: High-profile memecoin launches routinely leave retail buyers with losses, a pattern worth treating skeptically rather than as a real opportunity.
whatToWatch: Token price and trading volume trends going forward
Any regulatory or reputational fallout
questions: What was the mechanism meant to prevent the usual memecoin losses?
Who profited from the launch, and who lost?

stories.title: Jack Dorsey's Block seeks US trust bank charter for bitcoin and stablecoin business
stories.summary: Block, the company led by Jack Dorsey, applied for a US trust bank charter. The charter would support its bitcoin and stablecoin operations under a federal banking framework.
stories.whyItMatters: A trust bank charter would give a major fintech a formal regulatory home for bitcoin and stablecoin services, a significant step for the industry.
whatToWatch: The regulator's decision on the charter application
Details on which bitcoin and stablecoin services the charter would cover
questions: Which regulator is reviewing the application?
What is the expected timeline for a decision?
